what_this_is: An explicit, per-label curation ruling on the 42 :Devata nodes whose curated `structure` is ABSTRACT (41) or UNSPECIFIED (1). Agent 8's population audit flagged them and deliberately did NOT exclude them, leaving the call open on the ground that Sraddha is both an abstraction and a deity while abhisapa is not. This file makes the call, with a reason per label, so that it is reviewable and so that nothing is decided silently inside a pipeline.
the_rule_applied: Does the label name an addressee with a domain, or does it name the hymn's subject or its intended effect? That is not a rule invented here: it is the line DEVATA_TAXONOMY_V1 already drew in its sections 7 and 8, where `SPEECH` was reserved for deities whose domain is speech and withheld from bare ritual utterances, and where the charm-purpose labels were refused `HEALER` because 'the slot names the intended act, not an agent with a domain'. Applying the same line to the structure axis keeps one rule rather than two.
how_the_ruling_is_used: It is NOT applied as a silent filter. The partition is computed three ways -- with all 42 in (V-ALL), with the 28 NOT_DEITY rulings removed and the 5 UNDECIDED kept (V-RULED, the published partition), and with all 42 removed (V-NONE, the crude alternative) -- and the three partitions are compared by adjusted Rand index on their shared nodes. If the ruling barely moves the partition, the reader should discount it accordingly, and the proof file says by how much.
undecided_is_a_verdict: Five labels are ruled UNDECIDED and are KEPT in the published population. An undecided label removed is a decision made by default, which is the failure this file exists to avoid.

rulings.reason: RV 10.151 addresses her throughout in the vocative and petitions her; a hypostasis that the hymn treats as an agent with a domain.
RV 10.83-84 address Manyu directly as `manyo` and ask him to act; the theonym layer independently records 124 mention edges, the second-highest of the 42.
A named power who is propitiated and asked to depart rather than a theme; 70 mention edges.
Addressed in the vocative at RV 10.18.1 (`param mrtyo anu parehi`) and told to go elsewhere. An addressee.
RV 10.107 hypostatises the fee and praises her as a giver with her own agency. The underlying referent is an institution; the hymn's grammar makes her an agent.

The tradition's own reification of the interrogative in RV 10.121's refrain `kasmai devaya havisa vidhema`. It is a deity IN THE TRADITION'S READING, and the devata slot records the tradition's reading. Flagged, because a reader may reasonably hold that the hymn asks a question rather than naming a god.
RV 10.59 addresses her in the vocative as `asunite` and asks her for life. The English gloss reads like a process; the Sanskrit is a vocative.

rulings.label_en: Pathya Svasti, well-being on the road
rulings.reason: Invoked as a goddess of safe travel. Flagged for a separate reason: `pathya svasti` is also a metre name, so this key sits on the same deity-or-metre boundary that produced the 17 fused :Chandas entities in Agent 8's audit.

A deified animal. Kept for consistency: DEVATA_TAXONOMY_V1 carries thirteen animals in the population (gauh, asvah, mandukah, syenah, sarama and others), none of them excluded, and excluding this one because its structure is UNSPECIFIED rather than INDIVIDUAL would be excluding on a morphological accident. The taxonomy's own note says the label does not settle number, not that it is not a devata.

30 dedications across 4 hymns, the largest footprint of the 42. `atman` in these hymns is the subject reflected on, not a vocative addressee -- which argues NOT_DEITY -- but it is also the Anukramani's substantive ascription for those hymns rather than a purpose label, and 30 dedications is too much weight to remove on this agent's reading. KEPT.
The annastuti praises food and addresses it, which is an agent's treatment; but `food` is also plainly the hymn's topic. The two readings are not separable from the label alone. KEPT.

DEVATA_TAXONOMY_V1 names this entry as the one place it knowingly applied its own rule inconsistently, giving neuter `brahman` the SPEECH axis while refusing it to four ritual utterances. Inheriting the flag rather than resolving it: an agent cannot settle a boundary the curation file has already recorded as unsettled. KEPT.
The gloss itself is ambiguous between an act and a personified Bounty, and the label does not settle which. KEPT.
Read as a personified power in the later tradition and as an instrumental abstract in the Rigveda. KEPT.

rulings.label_en: the deities indicated by the wording
rulings.reason: THE MOST IMPORTANT EXCLUSION HERE. This is not an abstraction; it is the Anukramani's own deferral marker -- lingokta, 'stated by the characteristic mark in the mantra' -- standing in the devata slot as a node. Agent 8 counted 102 of these deferrals in Kathyayana's Yajurvedic sutra and treated them as unresolved. Here the same marker has been materialised as a deity and carries 3 dedications across 2 hymns. A community containing `the deities indicated by the wording` would be a community containing a null value. This node is a modelling defect, reported to the lead, not a curation judgement.
A theological gloss on Agni, not a second addressee. Including it would place Agni's self in a community beside Agni.

Names the hymn's subject. ALSO: this key and VG:DEVATA:BHAVAVRTTHAM are the same label spelled two ways, carrying 15 and 7 dedications; reported to the lead as a duplicate-entity defect independent of this ruling.
As above; the aspirated variant of the same label. The duplication is the finding.
Names the subject reflected on. No vocative, no petition, no domain.
RV 10.191's purpose -- that the assembly be of one mind. The slot names the intended effect.
An intended act.
Agent 8's own worked example of an abstraction that is not a deity. The hymn is against a curse, not addressed to one.
A charm-purpose label. DEVATA_TAXONOMY_V1 section 8 refuses this whole group an axis on the ground that the slot names the intended act; the same ground refuses it deityhood.
Charm-purpose label; same group.
Charm-purpose label; the taxonomy names this as the hardest of the group to refuse and refuses it for consistency. Kept consistent here.

rulings.label_en: the matter in the form of slaying a rival
rulings.reason: The label literally says `the matter in the form of` -- it names the hymn's business, not an addressee.

rulings.label_en: the matter in the form of subduing a co-wife
rulings.reason: As above; `rupo arthah` is the giveaway.

rulings.label_en: the matter in the form of implanting an embryo
rulings.reason: As above.
The desired outcome of a charm to bring back a departed mind.
Names an act performed for a named man. The taxonomy groups it with the charm-purpose labels and so does this.
An occasion. Surya's daughter and Soma are the parties; the wedding is the setting.
Names the verses themselves. A text is not its own addressee.

rulings.label_en: the blessings of the married pair
rulings.reason: Names the utterance. Grouped with the ritual utterances the taxonomy refuses SPEECH.
Names a rite. The Fathers are the addressees and have their own registry entity; the rite does not.

rulings.label_en: censure of the dice and the gambler
rulings.reason: Names the hymn's rhetorical act. The dice have their own entity (aksah) and it is not excluded.
A cosmological figure described, not petitioned.

An activity. Note the contrast the data itself draws: `sunasirau`, plough-and-ploughshare, IS a deified pair with its own entity and a TERRESTRIAL axis, and is not excluded. The implements are addressed; the activity is not.

A ritual utterance, refused SPEECH by the taxonomy for that reason. This is the costliest exclusion in the file: it has 9 dedications across 9 hymns and sits inside the apri sequence, so removing it changes the projection's densest region. Recorded as such rather than buried.
A ritual utterance; same group, named by the taxonomy explicitly.
A ritual utterance. Distinct from Pathya Svasti above, which is a named goddess; the plural blessings are not.

A praise label. Its own curation note in the registry reads `PATRON_PRAISE is withheld because no patron and no gift are named; this is praise of a reciter` -- so the curator's reason for not typing it PATRON_PRAISE was the absence of a patron, not the presence of a deity. It belongs with the seven PATRON_PRAISE exclusions in substance.

rulings.label_en: the hands of Bandhu and the others
rulings.reason: A body part of named human seers. Adjacent to the 22 HUMAN exclusions rather than to the deities.
